lines.text: Two computers. One desk. A Mac... and a PC.
The wedding video is on the Mac. The editing happens on the PC. Two point four gigabytes... on the wrong computer.
[sighs] So you hunt for a USB stick. Try to email it... too big. Upload it to the cloud... and wait two hours for it to come back down.
What if both computers simply shared... one folder?
Save on your Mac. Open on your PC. Put a file in the FolderBridge folder, and a moment later it's on the other computer. Even a video this big. And it works the other way around, too.
Connecting them takes one short code. Type it on the other computer, and they find each other. The only rule: both need to be on the same Wi-Fi network.
You see every change, from both computers. Edited the same file on both? FolderBridge keeps both versions, and lets you choose.
Deleted something by mistake? It's in FolderBridge's trash. One click, and it's back, on both. Nothing is ever lost.
And it never goes through the cloud. No account, no storage limit. Your computers talk directly, encrypted, on your own network.
In English, Hebrew, Spanish, French, Russian, or Arabic.
So put the USB stick away. Just save... and open.
FolderBridge. Free and open source, for Mac and Windows.
